title: Notable recent physics papers — arXiv daily batch, 19 November 2026
global_caveat: This is an inferred ordering, not an official arXiv trending chart; attention and citation evidence are limited for papers only just announced, so popularity cannot be measured reliably.

sections.title: First observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed decay Bc+ to J/psi D*+
sections.abstract: LHCb reports the first observation of this Bc+ decay at 5.4 standard deviations and measures its branching fraction relative to Bc+ to J/psi Ds+ as 0.067 ± 0.016 ± 0.003 using 9 fb−1 of proton-proton data.
sections.ranking_evidence: First observation at 5.4σ with a measured branching-fraction ratio and a public LHCb analysis record; placement reflects the direct experimental result, not citation momentum.
sections.claimed_result: The LHCb authors report the first observation and a relative branching fraction consistent with several predictions while disfavoring some higher predictions.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; LHCb proton-proton collision data from 2011–2018, 9 fb−1, reconstructed in two decay channels.
sections.unique_caveat: The statistical uncertainty (±0.016) dominates the systematic uncertainty (±0.003), and the reported quantity is a ratio to a normalization channel, not an absolute branching fraction.

sections.title: Light fermions can trigger a Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
sections.abstract: Lattice simulations of a vectorially coupled SU(2) scalar-fermion-gauge system without Yukawa couplings show evidence that lowering the fermion mass can trigger Higgs-like behavior, with a transition near a fermion-to-vector mass ratio of two.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed across lattice, phenomenology, and theory; data are available for replication; highlighted in the 18 November Antonio Marrone physics digest.
sections.claimed_result: The authors interpret changes in several lattice observables below a mass ratio near two as evidence that light fermions can trigger a Brout-Englert-Higgs effect in this model.
sections.evidence_type: computational; lattice simulations of an SU(2) scalar-fermion-gauge system.
sections.unique_caveat: This is not a demonstration of the mechanism in the Standard Model: the model uses vectorially coupled fermions without Yukawa couplings, the authors say the evidence is not definitive, and the transition's mechanism remains unexplained.

sections.title: A 10^5 solar-mass black hole in the bulgeless spiral galaxy IC 342: first stellar-dynamical measurement with Keck/OSIRIS LGS-AO
sections.abstract: Using adaptive-optics-assisted near-infrared stellar kinematics, the authors report a direct dynamical black-hole mass of (1.95 ± 0.61) × 10^5 solar masses in the bulgeless spiral IC 342.
sections.ranking_evidence: A claimed first direct stellar-dynamical measurement in a rare bulgeless-spiral setting, based on high-resolution Keck/OSIRIS observations; the authors note submission to ApJ.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer an intermediate-mass black hole of (1.95 ± 0.61) × 10^5 solar masses and argue that a radially varying stellar mass-to-light ratio is necessary to reveal its kinematic signature.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Keck/OSIRIS LGS-AO K-band integral-field spectroscopy, archival HST/WFC3 imaging, and Jeans anisotropic modelling.
sections.unique_caveat: The black-hole inference depends on the adopted dynamical models and on a young-population-driven mass-to-light gradient; constant-M/L models instead give only an upper limit.

sections.title: Discovery of a Massive Outer Companion to the TOI-178 Resonant Chain
sections.abstract: Combining astrometric anomalies, radial velocities, and high-contrast imaging, the authors infer a likely eccentric brown-dwarf companion to the six-planet TOI-178 system, whose five inner planets occupy a resonant chain.
sections.ranking_evidence: The claimed companion is supported by joint Gaia/Hipparcos astrometry, ESPRESSO velocities, and Keck/NIRC2 imaging; manuscript submitted to PASP.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' refined posterior favors a companion with semimajor axis 6.9 (+12.3/−3.3) AU and mass 21 (+47/−11) Jupiter masses; simulations find the inner chain stable over the tested interval.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Gaia DR2/DR3–Hipparcos astrometry, published ESPRESSO radial velocities, Keck-II/NIRC2 imaging, and N-body simulations.
sections.unique_caveat: The mass and eccentricity posteriors are broad because orbital coverage is incomplete; stability over the simulated interval does not rule out later instability.

sections.title: LEMUR: A Searchable Web Archive of Deep Chandra Images of Galaxies and Galaxy Clusters
sections.abstract: LEMUR releases uniformly processed Chandra images for 2,569 galaxies and clusters, alongside searchable morphology, photometry, downloadable data products, and open-source code.
sections.ranking_evidence: A reusable release of 5,505 Chandra observations totaling 138.8 Ms, with a public archive, Zenodo tables, and open code; cross-listed in astrophysics and instrumentation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors present a searchable archive and report that AstroCLIP-nearest cluster pairs share cool-core status in 73% of matched pairs, versus 51% by chance.
sections.evidence_type: observational; archival Chandra ACIS images reprocessed with CIAO, with AstroCLIP-based morphology search.
sections.unique_caveat: The release reprocesses archival observations rather than reporting a new observation; the morphology result and its 73% match rate apply to the archive's selected matched cluster pairs.

sections.title: Deconstructing the cosmic baryon distribution with fast radio bursts
sections.abstract: The authors combine FRB dispersion-measure modelling with galaxy-density estimates to reconstruct ionized baryons across cosmic-web environments in IllustrisTNG and a Euclid-like mock catalogue.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed in cosmology and high-energy astrophysics, accepted for publication in A&A, and included in a contemporaneous 18 November astronomy digest.
sections.claimed_result: In the simulation/mock framework, the authors recover ionized baryon density Ωb fion = 0.0455 (+0.0028/−0.0026) and reproduce bin-wise electron densities to within 10% of simulation truth.
sections.evidence_type: computational; IllustrisTNG magnetohydrodynamical simulations, Bayesian inference, and a Euclid-like mock galaxy catalogue.
sections.unique_caveat: The reconstruction is simulation-based and depends on the galaxy-tracer bias correction; deriving total Ωb additionally assumes an ionized fraction fion = 0.95.

sections.title: Observation of room-temperature intrinsic antiferroelectricity in van der Waals NbOCl2
sections.abstract: The authors report room-temperature antiferroelectric behavior in layered NbOCl2 and reversible strain- or electric-field-driven conversion to a ferroelectric state, tracked through optical signatures.
sections.ranking_evidence: Reports an experimentally testable room-temperature phase and reversible optical response, with cross-listing across materials, mesoscopic physics, and applied physics.
sections.claimed_result: The authors attribute stripe-like second-harmonic-generation signatures to antiferroelectric/ferroelectric phase coexistence and report a reversible response under an electric field of about 20 kV/cm.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; second-harmonic-generation mapping and angle-dependent measurements, Raman spectroscopy, and strain/electric-field control.
sections.unique_caveat: Phase identification relies on optical and Raman signatures; the abstract does not establish long-term cycling endurance or device-level performance.

sections.title: Map-Level Inference of Primordial Gravitational Waves from the CMB with Spherical Neural Networks
sections.abstract: A spherical graph-convolutional network estimates the tensor-to-scalar ratio directly from simulated multifrequency CMB B-mode maps and outperforms a bandpower-likelihood benchmark on the same simulation set.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed in cosmology and instrumentation; benchmarked against a likelihood on 20,000 simulations, with reported improvement in inference precision. This is a methods signal, not evidence of detection.
sections.claimed_result: On the authors' simulated experiment, the network lowers RMSE on r by a factor of 1.3 and produces 68% intervals 1.2 times narrower than the comparison likelihood.
sections.evidence_type: computational; 20,000 simulated multifrequency CMB maps with lensing, inhomogeneous noise, Galactic dust, and synchrotron foregrounds.
sections.unique_caveat: Performance depends on the foreground model; the authors report that generalization fails for a three-dimensional dust model with line-of-sight variation.
